problem_text:
A logistics firm must allocate a fleet of cargo planes to transport a selection of high-priority shipments across a three-day airlift operation. The objective is to maximize the total priority score of the shipments delivered, while adhering to the total allowable payload weight across the fleet.

The available shipments are:
* Shipment 1: weight 30 tons, priority score 190
* Shipment 2: weight 29 tons, priority score 84
* Shipment 3: weight 50 tons, priority score 256
* Shipment 4: weight 24 tons, priority score 42
* Shipment 5: weight 17 tons, priority score 299
* Shipment 6: weight 14 tons, priority score 79
* Shipment 7: weight 43 tons, priority score 279
* Shipment 8: weight 19 tons, priority score 51
* Shipment 9: weight 12 tons, priority score 12
* Shipment 10: weight 36 tons, priority score 285
* Shipment 11: weight 30 tons, priority score 294
* Shipment 12: weight 31 tons, priority score 152
* Shipment 13: weight 12 tons, priority score 12
* Shipment 14: weight 42 tons, priority score 232
* Shipment 15: weight 23 tons, priority score 164
* Shipment 16: weight 28 tons, priority score 34
* Shipment 17: weight 45 tons, priority score 26
* Shipment 18: weight 3 tons, priority score 137
* Shipment 19: weight 28 tons, priority score 56
* Shipment 20: weight 3 tons, priority score 202
* Shipment 21: weight 31 tons, priority score 117
* Shipment 22: weight 8 tons, priority score 146
* Shipment 23: weight 2 tons, priority score 98
* Shipment 24: weight 31 tons, priority score 34
* Shipment 25: weight 5 tons, priority score 19

A critical routing constraint dictates that exactly one of Shipment 1 and Shipment 2 can be accommodated.

Furthermore, if Shipment 3 is included, it necessitates specialized handling equipment that reduces the effective total payload capacity by 10 tons.
The aggregate payload weight across all planes cannot exceed 417 tons. The firm must determine the optimal set of shipments to load.
